deep.reconstruction:
This page holds four unrelated clusters of work. Each is restated below, with my own fill-ins marked [mine].

(A) Top left: the plane quartic (p=3) in Riemann's normal form.
- First expression: sqrt(x*xi)+sqrt(y*eta)+sqrt(z*zeta). Set equal to 0, this is the form of a general plane quartic Riemann used in his p=3 work (Werke XXXI). Here x, y, z, xi, eta, zeta are six bitangents.
- Under the three terms are characteristic labels: '0 a' under sqrt(x xi), 'b a+b' under sqrt(y eta), 'c a+c' under sqrt(z zeta). Measured from a base odd characteristic d (written as a partial-derivative-like symbol):
  - x = d, xi = d+a
  - y = d+b, eta = d+a+b
  - z = d+c, zeta = d+a+c
- Each pair therefore sums to the same 2-torsion element a. The three pairs come from one Steiner complex with characteristic a. This is exactly the condition for the eight contact points of any two pairs to lie on a conic.
- Second expression: sqrt(x eta) - sqrt(y xi) + sqrt((z+x+y)(zeta+xi+eta)). It regroups the four lines x, eta, y, xi into pairs whose characteristics sum to a+b (0+(a+b) = b+a). It then names a new pair of lines, z+x+y and zeta+xi+eta, completing a representation for the Steiner complex a+b.
- [mine] Rationalising on the curve: put X=sqrt x etc. Since sqrt(z zeta) = -(X Xi + Y Eta), one gets (X Eta - Y Xi)^2 = (x+y)(xi+eta) - z zeta.
- [mine] This equals (x+y+z)(xi+eta+zeta) exactly when z(xi+eta+zeta) + zeta(x+y+z) = 0. So the second expression presupposes a normalisation of the linear forms that is not written on this page.
- The following lines attach characteristics to the new lines, e.g. (d) = sqrt(z+x+y), d+a+c, d+a+b+c, d+c, d+b. They then list quadruples of characteristics, such as (d+a+b+c, b, c, ...), (d+c, c, a, a+b), (d+b, d, c, a+c), (d+a+b+c, a, a+b, a+c), (d+a+b+c, d+c, c, a+c). These are evidently groupings of bitangents into pairs and tetrads.

(B) Rotated prose, Latin and German Kurrent; fragmentary, my reading is uncertain.
- Gist: 'It therefore remains to show rigorously that what Gauss [established] for the composition of quadratic forms ... multiplication of negative determinants ... corresponds both to genera and to classes ...'.
- German: '...die Composition der quadratischen Formen mit negativer Determinante ...'.
- Bottom right Latin: '... formae quadraticae ... arithmeticae sublimioris ... perfecta sit, ostendendum est ... accuratius ...'.
- This is a prose draft about Gauss's composition of binary quadratic forms of negative determinant and its genus and class structure. No formulas belong to it.

(C) Middle: hyperelliptic material.
- Root functions (x-a1)(x-a2)*sqrt(x-a3)*sqrt(x-a4) and (x-a3)(x-a4)*sqrt((x-a1)(x-a2)), plus a normalised quotient (x-a3)(x-a4)/(a5-a4). These look like the products used to compare root functions at branch points.
- Index patterns (a1 a_m), (a_m a_1), (a_{m-1} a_m), (a_m a_2), (a_m a_1 a_2 a_3), (a_m a_{m-1} a_1 a_2) record pairings of branch points.
- Several sketches show circles and loops around numbered points 1–5 and 10, and rectangular cut systems. These are canonical cross-cut systems (Querschnitte) of a hyperelliptic Riemann surface, with loops around pairs of branch points.

(D) Bottom: a genus-4 hyperelliptic curve with 10 branch points 1,…,9,x (x = 10).
- 'ij sqrt(kl)' denotes (s-a_i)(s-a_j)*sqrt((s-a_k)(s-a_l)) and similar root functions.
- The four functions 34√12, 56√12, 78√12, 9x√12 are each split by the root factor √1 or √2 into 341/342, 561/562, 781/782, 9x1/9x2. These are named x, y, z, t and x1, y1, z1, t1.
- [mine] Then x/x1 = y/y1 = z/z1 = t/t1 = sqrt((s-a1)/(s-a2)). Hence the quadric relations xy1 - yx1 = 0 etc., which Riemann writes. The products xx1, yy1, zz1, tt1 are rational times √12.
- Characteristics are attached by the rows '0 b c b+c' and 'a b+c a+c a+b+c', i.e. a group of half-periods. Examples: a ↔ 34√12, b ↔ 1√3456, c ↔ 1√3478, b+c ↔ 1√5678.
- [mine] This is consistent with addition of characteristics as symmetric difference of branch-point sets. sqrt(3456)*sqrt(3478) = (s-a3)(s-a4)*sqrt(5678), so b+c ↔ √5678.
- Further triples (156, 246, 754, 8x127; 134, 236, 736, 89x) and lists of bilinear monomials (xx1, yy1, zz1; xy1, yx1, zt1, tz1; ...; xy1, xy, zt; x1z1, xz, yt; y1z1, yz, xt) set up quadratic relations among these eight functions. They look like the hyperelliptic analogue of the quadric relations among genus-4 theta/root functions on the previous page (ϑ(x±y)ϑ(z±t) products).
errors: The second quartic expression sqrt(x eta) - sqrt(y xi) + sqrt((z+x+y)(zeta+xi+eta)) does not follow from sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 for arbitrary linear forms. It requires z(xi+eta+zeta) + zeta(x+y+z) = 0 (or an equivalent normalisation), which is not stated on the page.

Some listed characteristic quadruples, e.g. (d+a+b+c, d, b, c), do not visibly have equal pair sums. Either the transcription or the intended grouping (pairs vs. tetrads) is uncertain, so no error can be asserted firmly.
In section D several sets (e.g. '6 sqrt(1524)', '4 sqrt(5726)', '8x127') are partly struck or illegible, so they cannot be checked.

results.what: Labelling the six lines of the form sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 by odd characteristics d, d+a, d+b, d+a+b, d+c, d+a+c, with equal pair sums a (a Steiner complex), and regrouping to obtain a representation for the complex a+b.
results.modern_name: Bitangents of a plane quartic, Steiner complexes, Riemann's normal form of the quartic
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (p=3 paper, published posthumously by Weber 1876); Steiner, Hesse; later Weber, Frobenius

results.what: Canonical cut systems on hyperelliptic surfaces drawn with loops around pairs of branch points, plus root-function products (x-a1)(x-a2)sqrt((x-a3)(x-a4)).
results.modern_name: Canonical homology basis of hyperelliptic curves; root functions / half-periods

results.what: Genus-4 hyperelliptic curve: eight root functions x, x1, y, y1, z, z1, t, t1 with proportional ratios, giving quadric relations xy1 - yx1 = 0, and characteristics labelled by branch-point subsets added by symmetric difference.
results.modern_name: 2-torsion/theta characteristics of hyperelliptic curves via subsets of branch points; quadratic relations among root functions
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann/Weierstrass school; Thomae (1870), Frobenius; Rosenhain/Göpel for genus 2

results.what: Latin/German prose draft stating that it remains to prove rigorously that Gauss's composition of quadratic forms of negative determinant behaves correctly with respect to genera and classes.
results.modern_name: Gauss composition of binary quadratic forms; class group and genus theory

deep.surprise_reason: The quartic and hyperelliptic characteristic work is consistent with Riemann's known posthumously published p=3 and theta-function studies. The Latin/German draft on Gauss composition of forms of negative determinant is an unusual number-theoretic theme for his Nachlass, apparently written beside theta-function work. But it is fragmentary and no result is stated, so it is at most a modest curiosity.

checkable.sympy: X,Y,Xi,Eta=symbols('X Y Xi Eta'); Z2=(X*Xi+Y*Eta)**2; expand((X*Eta-Y*Xi)**2 + Z2 - (X**2+Y**2)*(Xi**2+Eta**2))
checkable.asserts: Equals 0. So on sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0, (sqrt(x eta)-sqrt(y xi))^2 = (x+y)(xi+eta) - z*zeta.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,xi,eta,zeta=symbols('x y z xi eta zeta'); expand((x+y+z)*(xi+eta+zeta) - ((x+y)*(xi+eta) - z*zeta) - (z*(xi+eta+zeta)+zeta*(x+y+z)))
checkable.asserts: Equals 0. So the second expression on the page holds iff z(xi+eta+zeta)+zeta(x+y+z)=0.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,xi,eta,zeta=symbols('x y z xi eta zeta'); expand((x*xi+y*eta-z*zeta)**2 - 4*x*xi*y*eta)
checkable.asserts: The rationalised quartic of sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 has degree 4 and is tangent to each of the six lines (e.g. at x=0 it becomes (y eta - z zeta)^2, a perfect square).

checkable.sympy: s=symbols('s'); a=symbols('a1:11'); f=lambda *I: prod([s-a[i-1] for i in I]); simplify(sqrt(f(3,4,5,6))*sqrt(f(3,4,7,8)) - f(3,4)*sqrt(f(5,6,7,8)))
checkable.asserts: Equals 0 (for suitable branches). So characteristic b ↔ √3456 and c ↔ √3478 combine to b+c ↔ √5678 (symmetric-difference addition).

checkable.sympy: s=symbols('s'); a=symbols('a1:11'); f=lambda *I: prod([s-a[i-1] for i in I]); x=f(3,4)*sqrt(s-a[0]); x1=f(3,4)*sqrt(s-a[1]); y=f(5,6)*sqrt(s-a[0]); y1=f(5,6)*sqrt(s-a[1]); simplify(x*y1-y*x1)
checkable.asserts: Equals 0, verifying the quadric relation xy1 - yx1 = 0 among the genus-4 root functions.
Genus-4 hyperelliptic (10 branch points): 126 non-vanishing plus 10 vanishing even characteristics give 136; the 120 odd characteristics correspond to 3-subsets.

transcription_corrections: The labels under the first expression are '0 a' (under sqrt(x xi)), 'b a+b' (under sqrt(y eta)), 'c a+c' (under sqrt(z zeta)); the label 'a+b d' sits under the second expression.
The symbol rendered as '\partial' is Riemann's letter for a base characteristic (probably a Gothic/Greek d); it is not a derivative.
In the bottom block 'x' after 9 stands for branch point 10: '9x1', '9x2' = 9,10 with root factor 1 or 2; '9 10√12' = 9x√12.
'1√3456', '1√3478', '1√5678' are root-function labels (rational factor times sqrt of the product over the listed branch points), consistent with b, c, b+c.
The Latin 'in additione' is doubtful; the context ('formarum quadraticarum ... compositio ... generum tum classium') suggests 'in compositione' or 'in Disquisitionibus'.
The German Kurrent passage concerns 'Composition der quadratischen Formen mit negativer Determinante'; most other words are illegible.
The drawings are cut systems (loops around numbered branch points 1–5, 10) plus a two-circle figure. They are not number-theoretic diagrams.
